question.text: The two light beams having intensities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mi>I</mi></math> interfere to produce a fringe pattern on a screen. The phase difference between the beams is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi></math> at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math>. Then the difference between the resultant intensities at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> will be :

solution.text:
Resultant intensity is given by, Iresultant=I1+I2+2I1I2cosϕ

At P, IP=9I+I+29I×Icosπ2=10I

At Q, IQ=9I+I+29I×Icosπ=10I-2×3I=4I

Now, difference between intensities is 10I-4I=6I
